To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IE is an average of three rotated zero-linear trend (ZLT) regression models and that the orthogonal estimator (the OE) is the simple average of the three ZLT models.
(1) the IE and the OE are equivalent estimators, (2) the OE is a simple alternative that is more easily interpreted, and (3) both the IE and the OEs are not consistent estimators.
the IE is not a true linear model, it is not a true orthogonal estimator, and it is not the best choice for estimating APC effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
clarifying the IE and proposing a new estimator.
clarifying the meaning of the intrinsic estimator, examining its strengths and weaknesses in practice, and developing an alternative estimator that overcomes its limitations.
the identification problem in the IE and the development of a new estimator that is invariant to the number and size of the nonlinearities and is easily interpreted.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the orthogonal estimator is a better alternative to the intrinsic estimator.
the IE is a good estimator, but not as good as the orthogonal estimator.
the orthogonal estimator is a more appropriate alternative to the intrinsic estimator than the orthogonal estimator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IE is a useful tool for applied researchers, but its limitations should be recognized and the orthogonal estimator should be used as an alternative.
the orthogonal estimator is a more flexible and robust alternative to the intrinsic estimator.
the IE is a good estimator when the data generating process is a linear trend with a constant slope and the number of APC groupings is small, but the OE is a better choice for most other cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IE and OE provide different estimates and interpretations of age, period and cohort effects.
the IE is an ad hoc estimator that is not well suited to model nonlinear ageperiod-cohort trends.
researchers should not rely on the IE or any other APC model to identify a single set of age-period-cohort effects.
